login.title: Sign in
login.description: Sign in to manage this Allay backend.
login.forgotGame: Run /allay init in the game as an operator: it gives you a link that sets a new password, good for 30 minutes. Or ask another owner to set one on the Accounts page.
login.forgotHosted: Ask another owner to set a new one on the Accounts page. The admin from the backend's environment changes ADMIN_PASSWORD there.

errors.limited: Too many failed tries. Wait a few minutes and try again.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: How Allay is used and what it costs. Nobody's questions or answers are shown here.
dashboard.empty: No questions in this period yet.

charts.errorsHint: A cancelled question is one the player stopped, or that the plugin dropped.
charts.latencyHint: Over days, each point shows the upper bound of its time bucket.

dashboard.topPlayersHint: Who asked the most in this period.
dashboard.modelsHint: Runs and their cost, summaries included.
dashboard.toolsHint: How often the agent called each tool, and how often the call failed.
dashboard.noTools: No tools ran in this period.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everyone who asked Allay, newest first, by the name of their last question.

blocked.title: Blocked players
blocked.description: Allay doesn't answer them on the server named. Open a player to unblock them; a block outlives erasing their data.

erase.title: Erase a player
erase.description: When a player asks to be forgotten: their name, memories and places, deaths, settings, session, and agents' threads go, and their runs keep only numbers. Pick the player by name; a UUID or a pseudonym works too.
erase.noMatch: Nobody on this server has that name. A UUID or a pseudonym still works.
erase.confirmTitle: Erase everything about this player on this server?
erase.confirmNamed: Erase everything about {{name}} on this server?
erase.confirmText: This can't be undone. The audit log keeps that it happened, under the player's pseudonym.
erase.done: Erased {{memories}} memories; {{runs}} runs now count as nobody's.
erase.noMatchAnywhere: Nobody has that name. A UUID or a pseudonym still works.

player.description: A pseudonym: the same player always gets it. Their name shows once they ask again.
player.privacy: What the player asked, what Allay remembers about them, and their session stay theirs: the panel shows only names and numbers.
player.name: Name
player.nameLater: This player last asked before 6.4, when the backend didn't keep names. Their name shows after their next question.
player.hoursHint: When in the day the player asks, in UTC.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: Acts on the server you pick.
actions.resetText: Allay forgets the conversation so far, as after the player's own /allay new. Their memories stay.
actions.blockTitle: Block this player on this server?
actions.blockText: Allay stops answering them there until someone unblocks them. Erasing their data doesn't lift a block.
actions.unblockText: Allay answers them on this server again.
actions.unknown: Nothing kept on this server tells who this player is: no name, no consent, no memories, and their session has long expired. Erasing removes what's left, their runs and traces.

player.noServers: No questions on any server yet.

servers.title: Servers
servers.description: Every Minecraft server that registered or asked, with where players join and what it runs. Open one for its players and runs.
servers.internalHint: This server reaches the backend over a private network they share, so the address says nothing about where players join.
servers.noId: No server id: a plugin before 6.0
servers.playersHint: Everyone who asked on this server, newest first.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: Each question, wake, and summary with its numbers.

run.title: Run
run.toolsHint: Which tools ran and whether they worked; never what they were given or returned.
run.noTrace: This run has no trace: tracing was off or sampled it out, or its trace expired.
run.revealTitle: Open what this run was asked and answered?
run.revealText: Only to look into a problem a player or a server reported. The backend decrypts this one run for you, and the audit log records that you opened it and why.
run.revealReasonHint: What the player or the server reported, in 10–500 characters
run.revealed: What the run was asked and answered
run.revealedHint: Decrypted for this look only; closing the window forgets it. Each step shows what went in and what came out.

traces.title: Traces
traces.description: Traced runs with their numbers: who, where, which model, steps, tools, tokens, and timings. What was asked and answered stays encrypted; an owner opens one run from its page.
traces.none: No traces yet. They appear with the next question, unless tracing is off (TRACE_SAMPLE).

trace.title: Trace
trace.description: Each step of the run on one timeline.
trace.privacy: Model steps in blue, tool calls in green. What was asked and answered stays encrypted here; an owner opens it from the run's page.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.description: Telegram Stars payments. Dollars are estimates at {{rate}} a Star.
revenue.licenseCost: Runs on licenses cost {{usd}} so far

licenses.title: Licenses
licenses.description: Every license, what it may spend, and the servers behind it.
licenses.search: Search by id or server name

notify.title: Write to every license holder
notify.description: The bot sends this text to each license's Telegram chat, a few a second. Use it for a breach notice the servers' owners must get without delay, or news they need. The audit log keeps how many got it, not the text.
notify.done: Sent to {{sent}}; {{failed}} failed; {{unclaimed}} have no Telegram chat yet

licenses.lastsFor_one: Enough for about {{days}} day at {{pace}} a day
licenses.lastsFor_other: Enough for about {{days}} days at {{pace}} a day
licenses.lastsForHint: What's left divided by the average a day the open budget windows have spent since they began.
licenses.grantText: The money is there at once and lasts the given days, or to the end of what's paid if that's later.
licenses.extendText: Moves the end of the current period. The budget stays the same.
licenses.blockText: Its servers stop getting answers and can't pay until you unblock it. Operators see the subscription as inactive.
licenses.unblockText: Its servers can ask and pay again.
licenses.refundTitle: Refund this license and revoke it?
licenses.refundText_one: The bot returns {{stars}} Stars from {{count}} payment to the payer, stops the subscription, and revokes the license for good. Its key stops working: to use Allay again, the server deletes license.key, runs /allay link, and pays again or uses its own key. Its players' memories stay with the old license.
licenses.refundText_other: The bot returns {{stars}} Stars from {{count}} payments to the payer, stops the subscription, and revokes the license for good. Its key stops working: to use Allay again, the server deletes license.key, runs /allay link, and pays again or uses its own key. Its players' memories stay with the old license.
licenses.noServers: No questions from this license yet.
licenses.paymentsHint: A refund returns the Stars through the bot and closes what they paid for.
licenses.deleteText: Nobody's money is in it. The license and its budget windows go for good, and its key stops working at once. Its payments stay in the payments list.
licenses.paidText_one: Someone paid {{stars}} Stars in {{count}} payment and hasn't got them back. Refund the license first: the bot returns the Stars and revokes it. Delete it afterwards.
licenses.paidText_other: Someone paid {{stars}} Stars in {{count}} payments and hasn't got them back. Refund the license first: the bot returns the Stars and revokes it. Delete it afterwards.
licenses.forceTitle: Delete a paid license without a refund?
licenses.forceText_one: The payer keeps no access and gets no money back: {{stars}} Stars from {{count}} payment stay with us. This may break consumer protection law and Telegram's terms for Stars, and the payer may dispute it. The audit log records that you did it.
licenses.forceText_other: The payer keeps no access and gets no money back: {{stars}} Stars from {{count}} payments stay with us. This may break consumer protection law and Telegram's terms for Stars, and the payer may dispute it. The audit log records that you did it.
licenses.forceAgree: I understand the payer's rights may be broken, and I take responsibility for deleting this license without a refund.

errors.usd: Give an amount above 0 and up to 1000.
errors.name: Give a name of 1–64 characters.
errors.language: Use a code like ru or pt-br, or leave it empty.

licenses.editText: The name shows in the panel and the bot; the language is the one the bot writes to the payer in.
licenses.name: Name
licenses.languageHint: A code like ru, de, or pt-br; empty clears it. Telegram sets it when the payer claims the license.
licenses.budgetGroupText: Give money for runs, or move the end of what's paid.
licenses.accessGroupText: Stop the license's servers, or give the Stars back and revoke it.
licenses.deleteGroupText: Removes the license and its windows for good; its payments stay on record.
licenses.infinityText: Our own plan, never sold: a budget of PLAN_INFINITY_BUDGET for 366 days, from now. The license shows Infinity as its plan.
licenses.noWindows: No budget given or paid yet.

payments.title: Payments
payments.description: Every Stars payment and refund, newest first.
payments.refundText: The bot returns {{stars}} Stars to the payer, closes the period they paid for, and stops the subscription it belongs to.

import.text_other: {{count}} settings come from the environment. Importing saves their values here, so you can remove the variables afterwards. Until then, the variables still win.
